---
title: "If so, how far?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

The glide that follows from the built glider's own trim, set against the design's,
from the same release height.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Specified
1. **All-up mass: 16 g, balance point 15 mm aft of the plan's** · measured on
   the built glider by the user, 2026-08-30.
2. **Release height: 1.5 m** · as for the design, so the two are comparable.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Assumed
1. **Still air, and a glide already settled at trim.**
2. **The trim lies past the stall**, where `AeroBuildup` is reading NeuralFoil
   beyond the attached-flow regime it represents well. The range below is what
   the model says, not what the model can support.
:::

```{python}
H, BUILT_M, SHIFT = 1.5, 0.016, 0.015

x_np = neutral_point()
x_cg_plan = x_np - 0.10 * c_w
plan = trim(0.01550, x_cg_plan)
built = trim(BUILT_M, x_cg_built := x_cg_plan + SHIFT)
a_stall, _ = stall(built["V"])

# The two claims the prose makes without quoting numbers.
assert built["alpha"] > a_stall                      # as built, past the stall
assert plan["alpha"] < stall(plan["V"])[0]           # as planned, below it
```

**Answer.** The model says `{python} f"{built['LD']*H:.1f}"` m, against
`{python} f"{plan['LD']*H:.1f}"` m for the design — roughly
`{python} f"{(1 - built['LD']/plan['LD'])*100:.0f}"`% less, from the same
release.

**Do not trust that number.** The built glider trims *past* the stall, not below
it, so the flow is no longer attached and the section data behind it is a smooth
approximation to a flat plate — optimistic before the stall and unreliable after
it. Read it as an upper bound on what will really be
a nose-high mush, landing nearer the thrower than this, in a direction largely
decided by which wing drops first.

The useful comparison is not the two distances but their cause. The design flies
below its stall and the article flies past it, so recovering the distance is not
a matter of trimming for range — it is a matter of moving the balance point
forward until the aircraft is on the right side of its own polar again.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
show_source(trim)
```
